requirement_text: UNEDasiss is the UNED (Universidad Nacional de Educación a Distancia) service that manages access and admission of international/foreign-system students to Spanish universities. It evaluates a student's foreign academic record and issues a digital 'Acreditación' documenting a Spain-equivalent admission score. The service describes itself as 'Tu Puente a la Universidad en España' (Your Bridge to University in Spain).
source_authority_note: unedasiss.uned.es is UNED's official platform for this legally-designated national function; .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov, so fails the literal gate despite being the sole official body responsible for this process nationwide.
limitations: Page describes the service generally and carries no year label itself; year-specific mechanics verified separately (see deadline records below).
researcher_notes: Foundational fact for ORYN's international users: UNEDasiss, not a raw foreign grade or a national threshold, is what actually determines Spanish admission eligibility/score.

requirement_text: Students who can obtain UNEDasiss credentials to access Spanish universities directly (without needing separate degree homologation) fall into three categories: (1) holders of the European Baccalaureate title; (2) students with International Baccalaureate (IB) diplomas; (3) holders of 'títulos, diplomas o estudios equivalentes al título de Bachillerato del sistema educativo español' from EU countries or countries with reciprocal agreements with Spain.
source_authority_note: Official Comunidad de Madrid regional government education portal; .madrid domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov, so fails the literal gate despite being an official public-administration source.
limitations: Page carries no explicit cycle year; describes standing eligibility categories rather than a single year's rule.
researcher_notes: Directly relevant to ORYN's IB/A-Level/AP student segment: IB diploma holders and EU-country students are named explicitly as a qualifying category for direct credentialing.

requirement_text: Students from non-EU countries without a reciprocity agreement, or whose UNEDasiss accreditation does not include a recognized 'modalidad de Bachillerato', generally cannot be admitted in the ordinary (June) allocation round and may only apply in the extraordinary (late July) round, and only for seats that remain vacant after the first allocation.
source_authority_note: University's own admissions page explaining a UNEDasiss-system-wide rule; not itself the UNEDasiss/government source directly, but describes a national-level accreditation mechanic that applies system-wide, not just at UC3M.
limitations: This national-system rule is described via UC3M's own admissions page (not an independent UNEDasiss or ministry statement); wording may reflect UC3M's paraphrase rather than verbatim national regulation text.
researcher_notes: Important nuance for ORYN: holding a UNEDasiss accreditation alone is not sufficient — whether it includes a recognized bachillerato modality materially changes which admission round a student can compete in.

requirement_text: The Spanish undergraduate admission score used nationally runs on a 0-14 scale: a base 'Calificación de Acceso a la Universidad' (CAU) of up to 10 points, plus up to 4 additional points ('mejora de la nota para la admisión') from weighted subject grades (from PCE exams or recognized coursework, per each degree's own weighting table). For internationally-accredited students, the CAU itself is the foreign qualification's average converted to the Spanish 0-10 scale by UNED, as reflected on the UNEDasiss Acreditación.
source_authority_note: University's own explanation of the national 0-14 admission scale; consistent wording was independently found on UCM's and Comunidad de Madrid's pages too, but no single ministerial-order text could be directly fetched and verified for the exact original wording (see researcher_notes).
limitations: This is the standing national mechanic, not a per-year figure. The actual score needed to be admitted (nota de corte) is a separate, year-specific competitive outcome — recorded separately per program/year in the UC3M and UCM files, not here.
researcher_notes: Attempted to verify the originating national ministerial order/decree text directly on BOE.es for the exact '0-10 + up to 4 = 14' formulation. Real Decreto 412/2014 (BOE-A-2014-6008) was fetched and confirms the general access-and-admission framework (e.g. Art. 10.1: Bachillerato grade must weigh at least 60%) but the fetched excerpt did not itself spell out the 14-point ceiling — that specific figure is corroborated identically across UC3M's and UCM's own admissions pages plus Comunidad de Madrid's page, which is why confidence is still high despite not having the primary legal text's exact wording in hand.

requirement_text: Real Decreto 412/2014, de 6 de junio (BOE-A-2014-6008), regulates the conditions for access to official university degree studies in Spain. Article 10.1: 'La ponderación de la calificación final obtenida en el Bachillerato o estudios equivalentes deberá tener un valor, como mínimo, del 60 por 100.' Article 5.3: 'Las Universidades podrán realizar las evaluaciones que establezcan en los procedimientos de admisión en inglés, o en otras lenguas extranjeras.' Disposición Adicional Primera assigns UNED's normally-devolved regional-authority competencies directly to the national Government: 'En el caso de la UNED, corresponde al Gobierno el ejercicio de las competencias atribuidas a las Administraciones educativas.'
source_authority_note: BOE (Boletín Oficial del Estado) is Spain's official state gazette — the country's central legal-publication authority, equivalent in function to a .gov source, but hosted on the .es ccTLD rather than literally '.gov', so it fails the strict domain-suffix gate.
limitations: This decree provides general legal framework from 2014 and may have been amended by later orders not checked in this research pass. It does not itself state the specific 14-point ceiling figure used operationally today (see REQ-2026-08-21-0004).
researcher_notes: Included for legal-basis traceability per the task's source-traceability requirement. This is background/legal evidence, not itself an actionable student-facing requirement.

requirement_text: PCE (Pruebas de Competencias Específicas) exams are subject-specific tests organized by UNED via UNEDasiss, each lasting 90 minutes. Per a secondary source (educaweb.com — could not be independently confirmed verbatim on an official UNEDasiss/university page): each subject exam mixes multiple-choice questions ('Tipo test', answerable in English or Spanish) and essay questions ('De desarrollo', must be answered in Spanish); students seeking only to raise their admission score are recommended to sit at least 2 subjects, while non-EU students without a reciprocity agreement are recommended 4 subjects (some universities may require up to 6).
source_authority_note: educaweb.com is a third-party Spanish education information portal, NOT an official UNED/government/university source. Deviates from the task template's 'official_primary' default because this specific fact genuinely could not be located on an official page despite searching.
limitations: Secondary source only — the exam-format details (duration, question types, subject-count recommendations) should be re-verified against an official UNEDasiss page or the PCE examination regulations before ORYN treats them as authoritative.
researcher_notes: The registration/exam DATES for PCE (see deadline records below) were independently confirmed directly on unedasiss.uned.es/fechas_clave and are high-confidence; only this exam-FORMAT description rests on a secondary source.

requirement_text: The UNEDasiss Acreditación (accreditation document) is valid for two years from its date of issuance. The downloaded document is informational only — Spanish universities subscribed to the UNEDasiss accreditation system access the official record directly on the platform rather than requiring a transferred paper file.
source_authority_note: Confirmed via direct fetch of UCM's own official admissions page; university .es domain, not .edu/.ac/.gov.
researcher_notes: Practically useful for ORYN: a student's UNEDasiss accreditation obtained in, e.g., 2025 could still be used to apply for the 2026-27 or 2027-28 cycle within the 2-year window, without re-applying for accreditation from scratch.

requirement_text: Non-Spanish-speaking students coming from non-Spanish-language education systems must demonstrate Spanish language proficiency at B2 level ('nivel B2 de español') as part of the international access process. This was independently stated in near-identical terms on both UC3M's and UCM's own international-access pages.
source_authority_note: University admissions pages; treated as reflecting standing national/UNEDasiss-track practice since both Madrid universities state it identically, though neither page fully specifies the exact stage this is checked at.
limitations: Neither source specifies exactly which step (pre-registration, admission, or matriculation) the B2 Spanish requirement is checked at, nor the procedural consequence if a student cannot yet prove it.
researcher_notes: Do not conflate this with UC3M's B2 ENGLISH requirement, which is unrelated and is a graduation-stage requirement only, not an admission requirement — see UC3M file REQ-2026-08-21-1007.

deadline_text_verbatim: Convocatoria de mayo/junio: inscripción del 16 de marzo al 28 de abril de 2026 (puede sufrir pequeñas modificaciones).
limitations: Page itself notes dates 'puede sufrir pequeñas modificaciones' (may see small changes) — treat as provisional until close to the window. Independently corroborated on https://unedasiss.uned.es/fechas_clave.

deadline_text_verbatim: Exámenes en España: del 25 al 29 de mayo (de 2026); otros centros de examen internacionales pueden tener fechas distintas, a verificar en el resguardo de inscripción.
limitations: Applies to Spain-based exam centers specifically; international centers may run on different exact dates per the source page.

deadline_text_verbatim: Convocatoria de septiembre (extraordinaria): inscripción del 1 de julio al 22 de julio de 2026.
limitations: September session only runs at exam centers within Spain, per the source (the May/June session has international centers too).

deadline_text_verbatim: Los exámenes se realizarán del 2 al 8 de septiembre. La publicación de las calificaciones se realizará con fecha límite el 16 de septiembre.
cycle_label: PCE September 2026 session — exam window and results
limitations: An earlier WebSearch-snippet lead (not independently verified by direct fetch) suggested '20 de septiembre' for results — this was superseded by the direct page fetch's '16 de septiembre' and the unverified figure is deliberately NOT recorded here, per the rule that search snippets are leads, not evidence.

deadline_text_verbatim: Solicitud de acreditación: abre el 4 de febrero y cierra el 1 de diciembre de cada año.
cycle_label: UNEDasiss accreditation request window (recurs annually per source)
limitations: Source explicitly states this recurs 'cada año' (each year) on the same day/month; recorded as recurring rather than assuming the 2026 instance is a one-off. Page also lists platform closure windows (29 Mar–6 Apr, 1–15 Aug, 24 Dec–7 Jan) during which no processing occurs — relevant if a student's window falls near these.

deadline_text_verbatim: Plazo para solicitar admisión en universidades públicas para estudiantes internacionales que deseen iniciar estudios en el curso 2026/2027: 7 de julio de 2026 (con ampliación para aportar documentación hasta el 31 de julio).
cycle_label: General public-university admission deadline per UNEDasiss (2026/27 cycle)
limitations:
CONFLICTS with both UC3M's and UCM's own admissions pages, which each independently state the closing deadline for foreign-education-system applicants' preinscripción as '6 de julio (hasta las 14:00h)' 2026 — one day EARLIER than this UNEDasiss page's '7 de julio', and with an explicit 14:00 cutoff rather than just a date. UC3M source (fetched): https://www.uc3m.es/grado/admision/solicitud/preinscripcion — 'estudiantes de sistemas no españoles: hasta el 6 de julio (hasta las 14:00h)'. UCM source (fetched): https://www.ucm.es/calendario-de-preinscripcion — 'Sistemas educativos extranjeros: del 5 de junio a las 9:00h al 6 de julio hasta las 14:00 horas'. Both universities agree with each other (6 July) and both disagree with UNEDasiss's own page (7 July). Not resolved here — recording all three verbatim per the standing rule against picking a side. Possible (unconfirmed) explanation: UNEDasiss's figure may be a general/rounded national deadline while Madrid's Distrito Único (which both UC3M and UCM belong to) runs a locally-coordinated calendar that closes a half-day earlier — but this is speculation, not sourced, so it is NOT asserted as fact.

RESOLUTION 2026-08-22 (see docs/research/requirement-conflicts/05-spain-preinscripcion-foreign-systems.md): NOT A CONFLICT — the figures describe different levels of the system. Spanish university admission calendars are set by each autonomous community, not nationally. The Comunidad de Madrid's own access calendar (comunidad.madrid, retrieved 2026-08-22) states for sistemas educativos extranjeros: 'del 5 de junio al 6 de julio a las 14:00' — matching UC3M and UCM exactly, including the 14:00 cut-off. Both belong to the Distrito Unico de Madrid (Alcala, Autonoma, Carlos III, Complutense, Politecnica, Rey Juan Carlos), which admits on one coordinated calendar, so they are two restatements of one source rather than two independent witnesses. UNEDasiss is a UNED credential-accreditation service and owns no region's admission calendar; its '7 de julio' is a general national-level figure. Binding date for UC3M/UCM applicants: 6 July, 14:00. SCOPE: this resolution is specific to Madrid — other autonomous communities run their own calendars and must not inherit either figure. The UC3M/UCM/UNEDasiss pages were NOT re-fetched on 2026-08-22, so retrieved_at is unchanged; the new evidence is the Comunidad de Madrid calendar.
